transcript: Your speaker notes are written for you, not for a listener. Here's how to turn rough notes into a voiceover that sounds clear and natural.
Rough notes work on stage, but a voice needs full sentences. Instead of 'results, three groups, control flat', say: let's look at the results. We tested three groups.
A real script tells the viewer where to look, and links smoothly to the next slide.
Write the way you speak. 'Utilise' becomes 'use'. 'In order to' becomes 'to'. Keep one idea per sentence, because a listener can't scan back up the page.
Abbreviations, symbols and numbers can come out oddly. So 3.5% becomes three and a half per cent, and n=240 becomes two hundred and forty participants.
Narration takes its cues from punctuation. A full stop is a short pause. A comma, a smaller one. There was one exception. Low-light images.
Write full, short sentences, spell numbers as words, and read it aloud once. On Pro, a.i. directs the video, timing each scene to your words. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
